text:
Maya (eng-sre): Heads-up — SLO alert for `gpu-alloc-failure-rate` started flapping around 16:12 UTC. We're getting a huge volume of `alloc timeout` errors from `gpu-scheduler` and Kibana queries against corp-logs are timing out. Anyone digging?

Sam: saw it. Alerts line up with an autoscaler bounce in us-west-2. Kibana returned >100k hits for the last 10m, so dashboards are slow and the alert is noisy :/

Leo: can we sample at ingest instead of searching through everything? Current Vector pipeline is sampling per-event, not per-key. If we dedupe by `corr_id` or `alloc_id` we can cut noise.

Harper: also noticing Loki hot-shard in us-west-2 — `search_timeout` spiked. Might be related to large repeated log lines. Suggest routing verbose scheduler traces to a separate index temporarily.

Maya (eng-sre): Quick Kibana (KQL) I ran:
```
service: "gpu-scheduler" AND message: "alloc timeout"
```
This returns too many hits. We should collapse/aggregate by `corr_id` to count unique failures instead of raw lines.

Sam: Loki query that helps to see unique correlation ids (LogQL):
```
{app="gpu-scheduler"} |= "alloc timeout" | json | unwrap corr_id | line_format "{{.corr_id}}"
```
Then `count_over_time` on the result to see unique failing ops.

ingest-bot: alert: `vector-high-drop-rate` — sampling/dedup rules are currently dropping ~18% of incoming events in us-west-2. See https://alerts.internal/12345 :eyes:

Leo: For Prometheus alert tuning, consider switching to a ratio and a `for` clause to reduce flapping. Example:
```
expr: increase(gpu_alloc_errors_total[5m]) / increase(gpu_alloc_requests_total[5m]) > 0.02
for: 5m
```
That prevents short bursts from firing the SLO alert.

Harper: action items I propose: add ingest-level dedupe transform in Vector (key: `corr_id`, window: 1m), route debug/trace logs to `gpu-scheduler-debug-*` index with lower retention, and spin a temporary Kibana filter to show `unique corr_id vs total lines`.

Maya (eng-sre): sounds good. I'll add a Grafana panel showing `unique_corr_id_rate` and `total_lines` side-by-side so we can see noise vs real failures. Sam — can you open the Vector PR? Harper — can you check Loki shard IO and replication status? I'll coordinate the Kibana filters. Ping back in 30m with status. :thumbsup:

Sam: on it — drafting Vector patch to add a `dedupe` transform and a small sample_rate fallback. Will open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/6789 (WIP).

Harper: checking shard now — disk IO at 92% on one replica, moving replica to healthy node and kicking a reindex for older hot segments if needed. Will update here when done.

Maya (eng-sre): thanks. If anyone finds a high-cardinality label we missed (e.g., ephemeral thread ids) call it out — those are our usual Loki killers.

Sam: quick note: when you run the Loki uniqueness query, use a `|= "alloc timeout"` first to reduce scan cost before parsing JSON. Also consider adding a `label_format` in the pipeline to promote `corr_id` to a label for faster querying if it stays stable.

Harper: moving replica now. Will re-check dashboards after the rebal.

Maya (eng-sre): perfect — we'll reconvene after the PR + replica move. If the dedupe reduces noise, we'll update the SLO rule to use unique_corr_id metrics instead of raw error lines.

ingest-bot: info: temporary route `gpu-scheduler-debug-*` created with 7d retention for upcoming triage.

Sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/6789 — adds dedupe transform + docs. Please review.

Harper: replica moved, IO back to 45%. Kibana queries responding normally again.

Maya (eng-sre): awesome — thanks team. Leaving this thread open until we validate the SLO behavior for the next 2 hours.
